title: A line of text counts as an element: Size mode reads a heading or label, and a caliper across a label keeps its number off the words
goal: Pointing the Measure tool at a heading or a text label in Size mode shows nothing today, because text has no border for the tool to find, and a caliper drawn across a label parks its number right on the words it measures. Redliners measure text as often as buttons, so a line of text should read as an element: hover it for its width and height, click to keep them, and every number near it stays off the letters.
notes: Evidence: queue/audits/2026-09-02-legend-under-toggle.json rough 3 (headings are not detected in Size mode, so the walk used a Distance caliper), and queue/audits/2026-09-02-caliper-head-3-size.png where the 121 px pill sits on the word clipboard. ElementBounds.candidates requires a pair of horizontal boundaries that agree on 85% of their run (Sources/PhotonzCore/ElementBounds.swift, comments at lines 21, 55, 77 explain why glyphs are thrown out on purpose). A text line needs its own rule: take the LumaField ink band under the pointer, grow up and down while any column in the band has ink within the x-height step, then run left and right while gaps stay under the visible-gap width AlignmentScan.groupedByPixels already uses (8 logical px scaled). Offer it as a rung of the ladder so [ and ] still climb to the row and the card. Subjects for the readout come through CanvasNSView.subjects(of:) (CanvasView.swift near line 1291). Competitive: Figma and Sketch inspect give the size of a text box; Photonz gives nothing for text today.
acceptance: Try it: Photonz, Experiments window, release Next, flag next-measure-modes on (default). Open Tests/Fixtures (the settings-pane capture the audits use), press I until the pill reads Size, hover the General heading: it outlines as one element and a click commits its width and height as one undo step. The same works on a row label such as Launch at login.

A caliper whose feet land on the two ends of a label (Distance mode, or the Size commit) keeps its number off the words, the way it already keeps off buttons: the label is handed to the readout planner as a subject.

Flat background, a single word space and a hairline divider still read nothing; existing element detections on the fixture (buttons, switches, rows, cards, fields) are unchanged and their pinned values still pass.
Detection stays under 1 ms per mouse move on the fixture and lives in PhotonzCore with tests written first (fixture pinned in ElementDetectionFixtureTests).
Scripts/test.sh green; audit written under queue/audits/ with an offscreen render of the heading outlined and one of the label caliper; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task.

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) What a redliner gets from a line of text is its INK box: cap top or ascender to descender bottom, first to last glyph. A design tool would quote the text box (line height), but a screenshot does not carry line height, and the ink box is what a caliper laid by hand across the letters already says, so the two agree. (2) A button's label must NOT become a rung: the pinned tests and the audit of 08-23 say the pick may not flicker between a word and its button. A control hugs its label and centers it; a row label is left-aligned with the row's blank half beside it. So: words centered inside a rung not much taller than they are stay that rung's caption; everything else is a line of its own, innermost on the ladder, and ] climbs to the row and card as before. (3) Text on a photo or gradient is out of scope: the line reader needs one flat background behind the words and stays quiet otherwise. (4) Shortest version: one new rung read straight off the brightness field (ink band, run along the line while gaps stay under the visible-gap width), no font metrics, no OCR. Fixture geometry (image px, ink boxes): General 66..221 x 66..99 (156x34); Launch at login 98..278 x 181..205 (181x25); Copy to clipboard 97..308 x 662..686; word spaces inside a label are 9 to 10 px, letter gaps 1 to 3 px.

Built: Sources/PhotonzCore/TextLineBounds.swift (new) reads the line under the pointer off LumaField; ElementBounds.candidates puts it first on the ladder unless a control hugs and centers it (captionHeightRatio 5, centered within max(4, 10% of width)); detect/neighbors/subjects take textGap, the app passes AlignmentScan.visibleGap * pixelScale. Tests first: TextLineBoundsTests (12 scenes) + ElementBoundsTextRungTests (heading, row label ladder, button label, caliper subject) + fixture pins (General 157x34 px, Launch at login 181x25 px, Copy to clipboard as a caliper subject). Two existing synthetic button tests painted a LEFT-aligned label in a 200 px button (pads 40/100); they now center it, since a left-aligned label with room beside it is exactly what a row label is and is now its own element by design. aSettingsRowStillReadsFromOverItsLabel became level 1 (the row is one ] away). Optimized timings on the fixture: text reader 10 to 12 us, whole ladder 60 to 97 us per move, budget 1 ms.

Shipped in Next: TextLineBounds (PhotonzCore) reads the line of text under the pointer; ElementBounds offers it as the first rung (button labels stay the button), and Distance calipers get labels as subjects. Verified: 1353 tests green incl. 16 new core scenes + fixture pins (General 157x34 px, Launch at login 181x25 px); probe playtest Scripts/playtest/text-line.json; audit queue/audits/2026-09-02-text-line.json with renders. Optimized cost <100 us per move. Follow-up filed for the row-label width readout placement.
